query: For multicomponent high-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states at and near their high melting temperatures, what single testable methodological intervention could overcome the inability of EAM references to represent the many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid? Explain why it should improve reference–target phase-space overlap, predict the reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references, define the applicable composition and temperature ranges, identify supporting evidence from elemental or binary calculations, and specify a decisive free-energy benchmark that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Substituting the traditional EAM reference with a machine‐learning-based interatomic potential—trained on ab initio configurations sampled from both the solid and liquid phases near melting—will improve the reference–target phase-space overlap in thermodynamic integration, thereby reducing the path mismatch encountered in TOR-TILD’s EAM-based approaches.
generation.material_initial_state: Multicomponent high-entropy alloys (e.g., equiatomic or near equiatomic mixtures of five or more metals) in both the crystalline (solid) and disordered (liquid) states at high temperatures (approximately 0.85–1.0 Tm).
generation.intervention: Develop and deploy a machine-learning potential (such as a Gaussian Approximation Potential or a Moment Tensor Potential) trained on a comprehensive dataset of ab initio configurations sampled from both the solid and liquid phases. This potential would be used as the reference in thermodynamic integration instead of an EAM potential.
generation.conditions: Simulations would be carried out over the temperature range near the melting point of the HEA (roughly 0.85–1.0 times the melting temperature) and applied to compositions typical of high-entropy alloys (multielement systems with five or more elements in near equiatomic proportions).
generation.structural_mediator: The ML potential’s ability to accurately capture diverse local atomic environments in both phases mediates a closer alignment between the reference and ab initio potential energy surfaces.
generation.mechanism: By training on a dataset that spans the full range of atomic configurations in the solid and liquid states, the ML potential reduces discrepancies between the reference and target (DFT) energy landscapes. This enhanced expressivity improves phase-space overlap and shortens the thermodynamic integration path, thereby reducing the mismatch compared to EAM-based references.
generation.predicted_outcome: An expected reduction in the thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by approximately 30–50% relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references along with improved accuracy in calculated free energies.
generation.baseline: TOR-TILD’s EAM reference potentials currently used for thermodynamic integration in high-entropy alloys near melting temperatures.
generation.boundary: This approach is primarily applicable to HEAs with moderate to high compositional complexity (5+ elements) at temperatures close to melting. Its effectiveness may be limited in systems with strong directional bonding or in alloys where nonmetallic character plays a predominant role.
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of the mismatch reduction remains uncertain and will depend on the quality and breadth of the training dataset for the ML potential; the estimated 30–50% reduction is preliminary.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform parallel free-energy calculations using thermodynamic integration with (a) the traditional EAM reference (as implemented in TOR-TILD) and (b) the new machine-learning-based potential. Both calculations should be carried out on the same multicomponent HEA system across the targeted high-temperature range. The free energies obtained from the ML potential should be benchmarked against independent ab initio (DFT) free-energy calculations.
measurements: Quantitative comparison of the thermodynamic integration path lengths (or mismatch metrics) for the ML potential versus the EAM reference.
Deviation (in meV/atom) of computed free energies from direct ab initio benchmarks at corresponding state points.
Statistical assessment of phase-space overlap (e.g., via configuration histograms or order parameter distributions) for both methods.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the ML potential does not reduce the integration-path mismatch by at least approximately 25% relative to the EAM baseline, or if the free-energy deviation from ab initio benchmarks remains above an acceptable threshold (e.g., >10 meV/atom), then the hypothesis will be falsified.
